text: Composition builds complex objects by combining simpler ones, instead of inheriting from them.
Where inheritance is an is-a relationship, composition is a has-a relationship.
A Car isn't a kind of engine — a Car has an engine, so it holds one as an attribute.
[chuckle] Car's drive method delegates to the engine, calling its start and adding its own behavior.
So the car cooperates with its engine part, each doing its own job.
[sniff] The beauty is flexibility — you can swap the engine for a totally different one at runtime.
Here we replace the engine with an electric one, and Car's drive keeps working without any changes.
[sigh] The users of Car never notice — they just call drive, and the new part slots right in.
[groan] Many designers favor composition over inheritance, because loosely-coupled parts are easier to change and test.
